summary: Every SL/TP placement is preceded by query_algo_order_by_client, which maps only an error containing '-2011'/'UNKNOWN_ORDER' to not-found. Officially, -2011 is CANCEL_REJECTED and the query-not-found code is -2013 (the algo not-found code is undocumented). Any other response makes the probe raise or report unknown, so no protective leg is ever placed and every live entry ends in ENTRY_WITHOUT_PROTECTIVE + SAFE_MODE + entry cancel.
expected: A never-placed xa- id is reliably classified as absent using the exchange's actual response (verified on testnet), so the SL is placed.
actual: Probe with the real SDK BadRequestError(-2013) -> query_algo_order_by_client RAISES -> manager.py:743-744 returns (False, 'probe ...') -> SL never placed.
impact: Live trading is unusable (SAFE_MODE on every approval). With F-502, an entry that fills immediately is left without a stop.
evidence: manager.py:741-752 probe-first; binance_usdm.py:868 substring match; Binance error-code page: -2011 CANCEL_REJECTED, -2013 NO_SUCH_ORDER; the Query-Algo-Order page documents no not-found code; adapter_probe_out.txt.
why_tests_miss: All fakes return found=False directly; no test uses real binance_common error objects; the 09-04 testnet rehearsal is BLOCKED.
recommendation: Verify the real not-found response on testnet; map by exc.status_code; add tests that use real SDK errors.
known_prior: Partially: 09-REVIEW-FIX.md:42 asked to re-check the -2011 mapping in query_algo_order_by_client. That was never done, and its impact on every SL was not recognised.

summary: Cancel errors containing '-2011' are treated as an 'already canceled' success, but Binance also returns -2011 ('open order not found in the orderbook') for FILLED or expired orders. When the SL fails after an entry fills immediately, expire_pending_entry journals post_cancel and returns NO_TRADE while a live position has no stop.
expected: On -2011, query the order by client id. If it is FILLED/PARTIALLY_FILLED, run the emergency path (reduce-only close or protect, plus an alert) and never journal post_cancel.
actual: cancel_normal_order returns None on -2011 (probe). manager.py:561-580 then reports NO_TRADE ENTRY_WITHOUT_PROTECTIVE with only in-memory SAFE_MODE. cancel_untriggered_protectives likewise counts triggered SLs as canceled.
impact: An unprotected real-money position with a journal that claims no exposure. There is no alert (F-106) and the reconciler is cancel-only (F-952).
why_tests_miss: The tests model -2011 only as 'gone'; there is no cancel-of-filled-order case.
recommendation: Treat -2011 on cancel as an unknown final state -> query_order -> branch on status; match on exc.status_code.
known_prior: No; related: F-952, F-104, F-127(a), F-106, 08-REVIEW IN-10

summary: Every place_entry failure is treated as ambiguous. Definite rejections (-2019, -4164, -1021, -4061, -2010, -1111, -4014, -4023) leave no order, so the probe gets -2013, which is unmapped and raises. Every routine rejection therefore forces SAFE_MODE, ENTRY_ABSENT is unreachable, and the rejection reasons are lost.
expected: A typed error-code mapping: definite 4xx -> NO_TRADE with a reason code; probe only on network, timeout or 5xx errors; -2013 -> found=False (verified on testnet).
impact: An operational denial of service after any routine rejection, and NO_TRADE reason reporting is lost. No unsafe order is created.
recommendation: An adapter-level error taxonomy based on the A2 error table.
known_prior: KNOWN: 09-REVIEW.md:204 and 09-REVIEW-FIX.md:42/140 (-2013 deliberately unmapped); the wider taxonomy gap is new

summary: The adapter builds DerivativesTradingUsdsFutures() with SDK defaults: REST timeout 1000 ms, 3 retries, no API key, prod base URL and no testnet switch. Order POSTs time out after 1 s (ambiguous -> probe -> SAFE_MODE), and all signed calls fail without a key.
expected: One ConfigurationRestAPI built in a single composition-root factory, with a reviewed timeout (about 5-10 s), keys from the secret store, a testnet or demo base_path, and start-up validation.
actual: binance_common ConfigurationRestAPI(timeout=1000, retries=3, backoff=1000); the probe prints timeout_ms=1000 api_key=None; there is no ConfigurationRestAPI in src/.
impact: Live placement is unreliable or impossible, and ambiguous placements increase, which is where the F-501/F-502 risk sits.
why_tests_miss: Tests always inject a fake sdk_client.
recommendation: An explicit REST configuration factory, plus logging of the effective configuration.
known_prior: The credentials/testnet part is KNOWN (F-128); the timeout is new

summary: No recvWindow is passed and no server-time drift check exists (check_server_time is unused). The SDK stamps timestamps from the local (Windows) clock, so drift causes -1021 on every signed call. Through F-503 this surfaces as SAFE_MODE without a diagnosis.
expected: A start-up and periodic drift check; block entries when drift exceeds about 500 ms; an explicit -1021 mapping.
impact: An availability problem that fails closed but is not diagnosed.
evidence: binance_common/utils.py:116-119,413; grep recv_window/check_server_time in src gives only docstrings.
recommendation: Add a drift health check and a -1021 mapping.

summary: Backfill retries on both 429 and 418 (IP ban) with a short jittered backoff and ignores the SDK's retry_after. The cancel retry predicate retries any non-programming error (418/429/401/-1021). The X-MBX-USED-WEIGHT and order-count headers are never read.
expected: Honour Retry-After on 429; never retry 418 (global circuit breaker + SAFE_MODE); track weight; restrict cancel retries to transient errors.
actual: Retries into a ban, and blind cancel retries.
impact: A possible escalation of an IP ban (2 minutes up to 3 days) that also blocks the live and reconcile paths on the same IP.
why_tests_miss: The tests only assert that a retry happens.
known_prior: 08-REVIEW (the entry before IN-10) covers only the class-name fallback; F-122 (backfill has no caller)

summary: Every live SL/TP algo leg hard-codes workingType=MARK_PRICE, and the value is not recorded on the plan. Corrected Rule 15 requires CONTRACT_PRICE + priceProtect=false (both recorded) unless a mark-price backtest exists. Root cause: F-958/F-010.
expected: CONTRACT_PRICE as the default of a registered parameter, journaled on the plan.
impact: Live stop behaviour differs from the backtest and paper evidence (1m last-price candles).
recommendation: Make it a parameter; default CONTRACT_PRICE.
known_prior: KNOWN at planning level: F-958, F-010 (reported here as the code-level defect, per the STAGE C NOTE)

summary: Callback authorisation checks only effective_chat.id and never from_user.id, so any member of a group chat could APPROVE. APPROVE and SKIP are built as separate one-button InlineKeyboardMarkups, so a single alert cannot offer both.
expected: Check an authorised user id and/or require a private chat; build one keyboard with both buttons.
actual: A chat-only gate, split keyboards, and no APPROVE sender (M2).
impact: A low probability of unauthorised approval in a group, plus UX friction.
why_tests_miss: The tests use a private-chat fake.
recommendation: Add an authorized_user_id gate and a private-chat check; build one markup.
known_prior: F-127(d) (token not carried in the callback) is related but different

summary: After a decision, the original message is not edited and its inline keyboard stays pressable, so safety rests on replay, which is in-process only (F-126/F-127). Synchronous dispatch and DB I/O run inside the async PTB handler. Notify retries TimedOut (which may already have been delivered) and ignores RetryAfter.
expected: edit_message_reply_markup/text on a decision; offload DB work; honour RetryAfter.
actual: Stale buttons, a blocked event loop, and possible duplicate alerts.
impact: Double presses, loop stalls and duplicate messages.
why_tests_miss: PTB surfaces are explicitly not unit-tested.
